title: Opening; arriving in Chicago in 1927 with the Miramakers show
summary: Allen opens the session; Punch recounts reaching Chicago with a traveling show and settling with Al Wynn, Tiny Parham, Hughie Swift and Francois's band at the Golden Lily.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: This is September the 25th and it's an interview being recorded in the Howard Tilton Library, Seminar Room 2, Tulane University. Okay. Oh, and I better put my name on here. My name is Dick Allen.
What's your name? Prince Miller. Mine is Prince Miller.
Okay. Fine. Well, let's start up where we left off. Seems to me we were just getting you up to Chicago.
What happened when you got up to Chicago, Prince?

Well, I went in there with a big show from traveling on the road in the year of 1927. And the show was named the Miramak Miramakers. And after I got in Chicago, well, I struck all, struck luck there with fellas like Al Wynn, Tiny Palm, and Hughie Swift and all them kind of fellas. And I just got good there and made good. So I just stuck on, got to blowing around there. Got up together with a little fella called Francois Louisanans. He had been trying to get a band up together. So we worked together, say about five or six years, more than that. We worked at the Golden Lily five straight years. And the place caught a fire on a Saturday night, so that closed that job. But we still went on, playing different spots, swing lane.
